itr_form_reasoning: Taxpayer has capital gains (both STCG u/s 111A and LTCG u/s 112A) in addition to salary. ITR-1 does not permit any capital gains reporting; ITR-4 is for presumptive business/professional income only. ITR-2 is mandatory whenever there are capital gains and no business income.

regime_comparison.note: New regime wins, but the margin is narrower than a simple salary-only comparison would suggest because the taxpayer fully utilises 80C (Rs 1,50,000) and 80D (Rs 25,000) under the old regime, and total income (~Rs 13.3L) exceeds the Rs 12L new-regime rebate threshold, so the 87A rebate does not wipe out the new-regime slab tax the way it would for a lower-income filer.

capital_gains.grandfathering_note: DEMONIFTYIDX units bought 2017-08-10 (pre-31-Jan-2018): cost of acquisition for LTCG purposes = higher of actual cost (Rs 24,000) and FMV as on 31-Jan-2018 (Rs 33,000, i.e. 300 units x Rs 110), capped at sale value -- so grandfathered cost = Rs 33,000.

new_regime.rebate_note: Total income (Rs 12,08,000) exceeds the Rs 12,00,000 rebate threshold, AND per the amended section 87A proviso, the rebate cannot in any case be applied to tax on STCG u/s 111A or LTCG u/s 112A -- only to slab-rate income tax.

final_outcome.note: TDS Rs 65,500 vs final new-regime liability Rs 65,490 -- a token Rs 10 refund; essentially a wash. Illustrates that TDS deducted assuming a rough new-regime salary computation was very close to the actual liability once capital gains are added.

expected_preflight_findings.message: LTCG under section 112A (Rs 1,40,000) exceeds the Rs 1,25,000 exemption; Rs 15,000 is taxable at 12.5%.
One holding (DEMONIFTYIDX) was acquired before 31-Jan-2018 -- grandfathered cost basis (FMV as on 31-Jan-2018) applies instead of actual purchase cost.
Capital gains present -- ITR-1 cannot be used. Confirmed ITR-2 is required.
Section 87A rebate does not apply to tax computed on STCG (111A) or LTCG (112A), even when total income is below the rebate threshold -- a frequently misunderstood point.
